defects: The existentials over `p` and `P` are not linked: nothing forces `P` to lie over `(p)` (e.g. no `P.LiesOver (Ideal.span {(p:ℕ)})` or `P ∩ ℤ = Ideal.span {p}` constraint), so `Nat.Prime p` is a vacuous/decorative clause satisfiable independently of which ideal P is ramified — the statement's real content collapses to 'some maximal ideal P of O_K is ramified over ℤ', which is not the same proposition as 'there exists a rational prime p that ramifies'.
Uses the concrete `NumberField.RingOfIntegers K` instead of an abstract ring of integers `𝒪` satisfying `IsIntegralClosure 𝒪 ℤ K` as in gold, reducing generality.

Uses a different ramification predicate (`Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt ℤ P`, local at a prime ideal of the integral closure) instead of gold's `Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn 𝒪 (Ideal.span {(p:ℤ)})` (predicate on the ideal (p) of the base ring); the correspondence between the two predicates is not established by the statement due to the missing link between p and P.
